newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UK's Cunningham sees no quick end to EU beef ban.
newsitem.headline: UK's Cunningham sees no quick end to EU beef ban.

text.p: Britain's new Labour Agriculture Minister Jack Cunningham on Monday ruled out any early lifting of a European Union ban on British beef exports.

"The previous administration made the situation more difficult by the way they mishandled the situation and they have set back the agenda," he told reporters before a getting-to-know you meeting with EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler.

Cunningham declined to make any forecast for lifting the ban, imposed in March 1996 after the former Conservative government admitted that mad cow disease, or bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), could be caught by humans.
Conservative tactics of blocking EU business to get the ban eased ahead of an EU summit in Florence in June 1996 helped harden continental attitudes against Britain.
Cunningham said his meeting today with Fischler was aimed at setting the scene for the new Labour administration.
"I am not here to negotiate today. I shall be inviting Mr. Fischler to visit Britain later in the year," he added.
Cunningham said Britain wanted to establish a more constructive working relationship with the EU's executive Commission while pressing for changes.
"We have our objectives. One is reform and another is a lifting of the (beef) ban," he said.
